title: Every Sky Primitive Instance is tracked through the same four-directory lifecycle regardless of what it does
content:
Across A.6.1.1.1.2.1 and A.6.1.1.1.2.2, every Primitive Spark uses — Agent Creation, Prime Transformation, Executor Transformation, Agent Token, Executor Accord — is represented by an identical document skeleton: a Primitive Hub Document carrying a Global Activation Status, then Active Instances, Completed Instances and In Progress Invocations directories, plus a Hub Data Repository holding archived subtrees for **Failed Invocations** and **Suspended Instances**.

The repetition is the finding, not noise. The Atlas is imposing one lifecycle state machine on every governance mechanism: a prospective Instance is *invoked*, and per A.6.1.1.1.2.2.1.1.4 successful Invocations move into the Active Instances Directory while "failed Invocations are Archived" in the Data Repository.

Two properties follow. First, an Instance's status is always readable from **where** its document sits, so state is a location rather than a field that could disagree with reality. Second, failure is a first-class outcome with a designated home — failed Invocations are retained rather than deleted, which preserves an audit trail of governance attempts that did not complete.

The cost is verbosity: most of Spark's Artifact by volume is this scaffolding, with a large majority of units being directory stubs that carry no claim. That is the price of making every Primitive navigable by the same rules.
description: Hub Document plus Active, Completed and In Progress Invocations directories, with failed and suspended subtrees archived in a Data Repository — one uniform state machine across all Primitives.
